## Summary

I created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/FastDateParserAgentTest.java` with 37 self-contained JUnit 5 tests covering `FastDateParser`'s construction, parsing, equality, century/two-digit-year handling, numeric field width constraints, quoted literals, locale-specific text/timezone strategies, serialization, and error handling.

36 tests pass. One test fails and shows a genuine bug in the code:

- **`testTwoLetterZPatternAcceptsRfc822FormatLikeSimpleDateFormat`** — `FastDateParser`'s javadoc states "all patterns are compatible with SimpleDateFormat." For the pattern letter `Z`, real `SimpleDateFormat` treats 1, 2, and 3 occurrences identically, accepting the plain RFC 822 offset format (e.g. `-0800`) and rejecting the colon form (`-08:00`). In `FastDateParser.getStrategy()` (`FastDateParser.java` around line 967), there's a special case: `if (width == 2) return ISO8601TimeZoneStrategy.ISO_8601_3_STRATEGY;` — this makes the two-letter `ZZ` pattern require the colon form (`-08:00`) and reject the standard `-0800` form that `SimpleDateFormat` (and `Z`/`ZZZ`/`ZZZZ` in `FastDateParser` itself) accept. This breaks the documented drop-in compatibility specifically for the two-`Z` pattern.
